independence_rule: Facts were established from the local Book III chapter text before comparison with production JSON. Canonical IDs are normalization labels only. Character identity claims are distinct from narrative identity.

chapters.title: Sasaki Kojirō
referenced_characters: kojiro: certificate name only, not the dead bearer's established identity

facts.description: Matahachi works at the Fushimi Castle works and becomes ill from heat and exhaustion.
A wandering student warrior gives Matahachi medicine and asks him to warn if anyone approaches.
The traveler sketches Fushimi Castle and its approaches; an inspector attempts to detain him.
The traveler kills the inspector and is then overwhelmed, bound and mortally wounded by workers and guards.
The dying traveler struggles to communicate a request; after his death Matahachi takes his bundle, money, pillbox and papers.
Fearing arrest, Matahachi flees and hides in a deserted house in Fushimi.
A mendicant priest laments his lost samurai status, his conduct involving Otsū and the harm done to his only son Jōtarō.
Matahachi finds a Chūjō-style certificate addressed to Sasaki Kojirō and issued by Kanemaki Jisai.
Matahachi incorrectly assumes the dead certificate bearer must have been Sasaki Kojirō.

chapters.title: Reunion in Osaka
referenced_characters: kojiro: false identity deliberately claimed by Matahachi
historical_context: Toyotomi Hideyori and Osaka rōnin recruitment

facts.description: Aoki and Matahachi fight in the deserted house; Aoki demonstrates substantial martial skill.
The priest says he was born in Himeji, formerly served as a samurai and begins to say his name as 'Aoki Tan-' before retracting it.
Matahachi travels toward Osaka seeking people connected to Kanemaki Jisai so he can identify the certificate's intended owner.
Matahachi tells Yasoma that he is Sasaki Kojirō and claims Jisai's lineage as his own.
Yasoma takes Matahachi's money while pretending he can secure an Osaka position for him; Matahachi later learns he is a swindler.
During a gambler confrontation Matahachi again publicly identifies himself as Sasaki Kojirō.
Matahachi unexpectedly encounters Osugi and Gonroku at the tiger sideshow and is caught by his mother.
When the certificate's Sasaki Kojirō name is exposed, Matahachi lies that it is his nom de guerre.
After Osugi's distorted account of events in Miyamoto, Matahachi agrees to join the revenge against Musashi and Otsū.

chapters.title: The Handsome Young Man
physical_locations: ship crossing the Inland Sea from Awa/Shikoku toward Osaka

facts.description: The true Kojirō recounts his Tomita training, four years under Kanemaki Jisai, return to Iwakuni for his dying mother and independent long-sword training.
Kojirō identifies his inherited three-foot sword as the Drying Pole.
Kojirō says Kusanagi Tenki holds Jisai's certificate, secret-method book and money, with a meeting planned at Mount Hōraiji.
Kojirō and Tōji dispute the Yoshioka reputation; Tōji reveals his identity and status.
Kojirō cuts off Tōji's topknot without injuring his head.
Kojirō's monkey steals the merchants' cards and climbs the mast.
The captain fires a musket at the monkey; Kojirō pushes the barrel aside so the shot misses.
Kojirō challenges the captain's authority and the merchants' behavior.

chapters.title: The Seashell of Forgetfulness
historical_context: Sumiyoshi poetic tradition and the seashell of forgetfulness

facts.description: Kojirō disembarks at Kizugawa with the monkey physically on his shoulder and leaves the harbor.
Oko meets Tōji at the harbor and takes him toward the Sumiyoshi inn.
At the inn the missing topknot and Kojirō incident become known to the Yoshioka party.
Yoshioka disciples decide to find the young swordsman with the monkey and avenge the school's honor.
Akemi searches for the seashell of forgetfulness, explicitly thinks of Musashi and wishes she could forget her past and Seijūrō.
Seijūrō isolates Akemi and sexually assaults her despite her explicit resistance; she later flees in shock.
Matahachi quarrels with Osugi during the shrine visit and leaves her and Gonroku.
Akemi walks deliberately into deep water intending to die.
Gonroku rescues Akemi but drowns and cannot be revived.
Osugi remains with Gonroku's body and desperately tries to revive him.
Seijūrō stays beside feverish Akemi at the inn.
In delirium Akemi mentions Musashi, New Year's and Gojō Bridge, revealing the expected meeting.
Ryōhei arrives from Kyoto with Musashi's written challenge to the House of Yoshioka.
Seijūrō entrusts Akemi to the innkeeper, takes Ryōhei's horse and departs toward Kyoto while Ryōhei follows on foot.
Seven Yoshioka disciples trace Kojirō from an Osaka swordsmith to Temma and pursue his ferry toward Kema.
The pursuers challenge Kojirō from the bank; he forces the ferry toward Kema rather than evade them.
Kojirō lands and kills or disables several pursuing disciples; the monkey contributes to the initial disruption.
Seijūrō and Ryōhei arrive and encounter the surviving disciples and Kojirō.
Ryōhei attacks Kojirō, misses and falls into the paddy field.
Seijūrō identifies the young swordsman as Sasaki Kojirō/Ganryū through reputation and his connection to Itō Yagorō.
Kojirō accepts Seijūrō's invitation to stay with the Yoshioka household in Kyoto.
They continue upstream toward Kyoto with the surviving disciples.

chapters.title: Eagle Mountain
referenced_characters: Shishido Baiken: kohei identity not yet revealed

facts.description: Musashi rides with a hired groom from the Kuwana/Tarusaka area toward Yokkaichi and Ujii while an infected foot worsens.
Musashi and the groom reach Baiken's smithy; Baiken is absent, while his wife, Iwa and infant are present.
Baiken's wife demonstrates a Yaegaki chain-sickle stance.
The groom takes Musashi onward to Yamada near Ise Shrine.
An inquiry to the Arakida house reports that Baiken is not staying there.
Musashi's infected foot and fever worsen; after failed remedies he leaves the inn rather than remain bedridden before the Yoshioka deadline.
Musashi leaves his swords and pack at the House of Virgins before purification.
Musashi breaks the ice and immerses himself in the Isuzu River, then follows the upper river and climbs to Eagle Mountain.
Musashi reaches the summit, experiences a psychological breakthrough and the abscess in his foot drains.
Shrine maidens find Musashi's pack and swords; Otsū takes them to Arakida without recognizing their owner.
Otsū and Jōtarō have spent roughly two months at Ise after searching the Iga, Omi and Mino routes for Musashi.
Otsū confronts Jōtarō for practicing on sacred trees and they discuss the shrine's decline and history.
Arakida says gossip about Otsū's chastity makes her residence among the shrine maidens controversial; she agrees to leave.
Arakida entrusts Otsū with painted scrolls for Karasumaru Mitsuhiro and provides travel money.
An unidentified man claims Musashi's pack and swords; Arakida authorizes release against a receipt.
Jōtarō chases a limping traveler who resembles Musashi but concludes he is not his teacher.
Otsū and Jōtarō leave Ise for Kyoto carrying Arakida's scrolls.
With his foot largely healed, Musashi crosses to Ōminato and disembarks at Tsu.
At Tsu Musashi notices a chain-sickle-carrying blacksmith and Iwa, follows them and confirms the man is Shishido Baiken.
Baiken returns home with Iwa and a pinwheel for the infant; Musashi stays at the smithy.
Baiken drinks with Musashi and explains chain-sickle tactics while pressing him to drink heavily.
Baiken learns Musashi was formerly Takezō and fought at Sekigahara, linking him to Temma's death.
Baiken and about ten armed associates attempt to kill the apparently sleeping Musashi.
Musashi detects the ambush from the pinwheel, opens a door as misdirection and hides inside under a rain cape.
The narration explicitly identifies Shishido Baiken as Tsujikaze Kōhei and confirms Tsujikaze Temma was his brother.
Musashi chooses not to kill sleeping Kōhei and lays Kōhei's wrapped blade across his neck as proof he could have done so, then leaves.
Otsū and Jōtarō resume the journey, passing Mount Fudesute and reaching Yonkenjaya.
Otsū rents a horse and Jōtarō rides it.
Baiken overtakes them, says he is pursuing Musashi and demands their horse; they refuse.
Otsū draws Baiken's sword; he loses fingertips; the horse is cut and bolts with Jōtarō, separating him from Otsū.
Baiken catches Otsū and hands her to associates to be taken toward Yasugawa.
Jōtarō escapes the bolting horse by grabbing a branch and turns back to search for Otsū.
Sannojō falsely reports Musashi waiting below for battle and manipulates the captors into leaving Otsū tied to a tree; Jōtarō frees her.
Sannojō guides them above Kaga Village to Makado Pass and directs them toward Seto in Otsu.
At parting Sannojō hints at romantic or marriage interest in Otsū.
Otsū and Jōtarō continue via Omi, Seta and Keage to Kyoto, planning to deliver Arakida's scrolls and await Musashi at Gojō Bridge.

chapters.title: The Butterfly in Winter
historical_context: New Year's Kyoto and Toribe funerary landscape

facts.description: Akemi secretly leaves Sumiyoshi, travels up the Yodo to Kyoto and reaches the Teramachi/Gojō area while hoping to see Musashi.
Yasoma follows Akemi into a field near Toribe Hill, throws her down and attempts to assault her.
Aoki intervenes with his shakuhachi, knocks Yasoma unconscious and rescues Akemi.
Aoki shelters and feeds feverish Akemi and hears her history and Seijūrō's violence.
Kojirō's missing monkey appears inside Aoki's temple.
Kojirō and Seijūrō hunt nearby; Kojirō searches for his missing monkey while Seijūrō worries about the Musashi duel.
The hunting dog attacks the monkey and bites Akemi; Kojirō kills the dog and treats Akemi's bleeding wound.
Kojirō takes Akemi and the recovered monkey away to care for her.
Aoki returns, finds Akemi gone and learns a young samurai carried away Akemi and the monkey.

chapters.title: The Announcement
historical_context: New Year's Eve 1605 as stated by the announcement

facts.description: Creditors crowd the Yoshioka school while Seijūrō hides and Ryōhei drives them out by intimidation.
The chapter reports that Gion Tōji disappeared with Oko and western-trip funds, while Denshichirō is absent and indebted.
Seijūrō and followers set the Musashi duel for Rendaiji field at seven in the morning on the ninth day of the first month.
Ryōhei and companions post the written response at Gojō Bridge.
Musashi searches Yoshida Hill for his maternal aunt, his closest living relative besides Ogin.
Musashi meets his aunt and her husband Matsuo Kaname, who confront him with Osugi's accusations.
Musashi learns Osugi has repeatedly visited the household seeking information about him.
On New Year's morning Osugi attacks Musashi near Gojō Bridge and refuses his attempts to explain or wait for Matahachi.
Osugi's blow needles irritate Musashi's eye and her blade scratches his forearm; he recognizes his underestimation as a tactical failure.
Musashi disarms Osugi, carries her to a boat under the bridge and restrains her while waiting for Matahachi.

chapters.title: The Great Bridge at Gojō Avenue
historical_context: New Year's visits and worship in Kyoto
referenced_locations: Zuzuya inn near Rokujō Avenue monastery

facts.description: Musashi discovers the pain in his eye came from triangular blow needles fired by Osugi and revises his skepticism about the weapon.
Akemi reaches Musashi at the bridge, gives him cloth for his eye and is recognized as the girl from Ibuki.
Akemi tells Musashi about her suffering and sexual violation while insisting that her emotional fidelity remains unchanged.
Musashi and the true Sasaki Kojirō see one another for the first time and silently assess each other's martial presence.
Akemi tells Musashi the watching swordsman is Sasaki Kojirō, also called Ganryū.
Musashi sends Akemi back toward her lodging with Kojirō and promises to visit; Kojirō leaves laughing.
Otsū sees Musashi embracing and speaking with Akemi from behind an oxcart; Jōtarō finds her hiding and upset.
After Akemi leaves, Otsū and Jōtarō try to catch Musashi, but he crosses the river and disappears before Otsū reaches him.
When Matahachi fails to appear, Musashi releases Osugi and urges her to seek her son rather than pursue revenge.
Osugi spots and pursues Otsū and struggles physically with Jōtarō when he intervenes.
Osugi claims she has forgiven Otsū and manipulates Jōtarō into persuading Otsū that it is safe to talk.
Believing reconciliation with Matahachi proper, Otsū agrees to help Osugi search for him and goes with her toward the Sannen Hill inn.
A crowd reads the Yoshioka announcement and Musashi's name begins spreading among previously unaware townspeople.
